question: When millions of people use the same AI model, whose values should guide how it answers hard moral questions?
reflection: Inviting many cultures and faiths to shape how AI reasons can help these tools respect the people they serve.

sources.subject: Anthropic is giving Claude a constitution
OpenAI cut GPT-6.1 Sol input cost to $0.10/M tokens: here's the trade

one_line: Questions about whose values guide AI models grow louder, as OpenAI pushes into office software and cheaper near-flagship models.

top_stories.title: Who writes an AI model's moral rules?
top_stories.what: Anthropic guides Claude with a written constitution and has asked religious, philosophical and cultural groups for input on hard moral choices.
top_stories.why: Value choices made by one company reach users everywhere, so local cultural input and public review matter for countries like Saudi Arabia.

top_stories.title: OpenAI launches its own office tools
top_stories.what: OpenAI released a shared workspace for people and agents, a documents tool and a slide tool, putting ChatGPT in direct competition with established office suites.
top_stories.why: Organisations will soon choose between office suites partly by their AI features, which raises training and data-governance questions.

top_stories.title: Near-flagship quality at a fifth of the price
top_stories.what: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Sol, which it says nearly matches its top model on coding and document work at about one fifth of the cost, plus a fast API for picking from fixed options.
top_stories.why: Lower costs make it realistic to analyse large volumes of reports or open survey answers on a modest research budget.

saudi_lens.text: As AI labs consult cultural and religious communities on model values, Saudi institutions could offer structured input so that widely used models reflect Arabic and Islamic perspectives fairly.

idea.title: Local values test for AI models
idea.pitch: Build a set of culturally grounded moral and social questions and compare how leading models answer them for Saudi users.
idea.first_step: Draft twenty everyday scenarios on family, community and work, reviewed by a small local panel.

idea_kids.title: Our class rules for a robot
idea_kids.pitch: Children write a short set of rules for a classroom robot helper, then test them with tricky situations acted out by classmates.
idea_kids.first_step: Prepare ten tricky situation cards, such as a friend asking the robot to share a secret.
